title: One Tap, One Charge: Optimizing Action Buttons
summary: This reel demonstrates best practices for handling button states during asynchronous operations, such as payment processing. It covers techniques like instant disabling, layout-stable spinners, idempotency keys, and response-driven state changes to ensure a robust and user-friendly experience.

transcript.text: The moment it's tapped, the button disables itself instantly.
A slow network shouldn't let you buy a second time.
Swap the label for a spinner inside the same button.
With the width locked, so nothing around it jumps.
Disabling the UI isn't enough on its own.
Guard the handler directly in your own code.
Hand the server a real idempotency key.
On success, morph the spinner into a check for a full beat before moving the user along.
On error, snap back and say why, right there on the button.
Re-enable only after the real request resolves.
Not on a timer, not on a guess.
Go to designmotionhq.com for more, link in bio.

on_screen_text: UI off isn't enough. Guard it.
Land on a check or an error.
Resolve to a check or an error.
On the response, not a timer.
before_after: Comparison of layout shifts (reflows) versus locked-width buttons, and timer-based versus response-based button re-enabling.
